pages.title: Tatami and Tatami Mats
pages.text: Tatami mats are made for Gensokyo-style rooms. Place one while holding at least two and the pair joins into a connected two-part mat for a neat floor; with only one in hand, or no room in front of you, a single square mat goes down instead. Breaking a pair separates it again and each half gives a mat back. The full-height tatami block pairs the same way. Both are woven from hay and string, and a block stonecuts into eight mats.

pages.title: Cabinets
pages.text: Two cabinets of twenty-seven slots each, one with drawers and one with two doors. Right-click to open the storage. Sneak-right-click instead swings the front open or shut without taking anything out. Either one stonecuts straight from a dark oak log, and both count as storage when a room is being measured for a home.

pages.title: Cartons, Crates and Books
pages.text: $(bold)Cartons.$() Plain, white and blue, all the same low open crate. Six paper makes two, and dyeing one gives you the others.$(br2)$(bold)Crates.$() A full block. Stonecut it from dark oak planks, or build one from planks and sticks.$(br2)$(bold)Books.$() A pile and a stack both come from five books. A pile lies flat in three sizes, and you can click it to cycle between them. A stack stands upright, and string ties it into a bundle that shears can open again. Neither gives the block back when broken: a pile returns five books, a stack six.
